children: Shares of automobile companies came under pressure on Wednesday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, with investors assessing the potential impact of higher borrowing costs on vehicle demand.

The Nifty Auto index emerged as the worst-performing sectoral index during the session, with all its constituents trading in the red. Ashok Leyland led the decline, falling as much as 3.5 per cent. Bajaj Auto, Tube Investments of India, Bharat Forge, Hyundai Motor India and Hero MotoCorp declined between 2 per cent and 3 per cent following the policy announcement.

The rate increase comes at a crucial point for automobile manufacturers, with the industry entering the festive demand period. The festive season is expected to contribute to third-quarter sales this year, compared with the second quarter last year, making the strength of bookings over the coming weeks particularly important for manufacturers and dealers.
Higher Financing Costs Cloud Demand Outlook

The immediate concern for the sector is the potential transmission of higher policy rates into retail borrowing costs. Banks can reprice loans linked to external benchmarks, including the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR), increasing the cost of vehicle financing for consumers.

For buyers dependent on financing, higher interest rates translate into larger equated monthly instalments (EMIs). This could encourage some prospective buyers to postpone purchases in anticipation of lower borrowing costs, potentially affecting enquiries and bookings at dealerships.
The impact could be more significant for segments where financing plays a larger role in purchase decisions, particularly commercial vehicles and entry-level passenger vehicles.
The rate-driven selling adds to weakness in auto stocks following September vehicle sales, which fell short of analyst expectations for several companies.

Bajaj Auto was among the biggest laggards after its September sales numbers disappointed the market. The sector had already been facing concerns over the pace of demand recovery, making the festive sales period an important test for manufacturers.
With the RBI now signalling higher borrowing costs, investors will be watching whether festive demand can offset the potential pressure from more expensive vehicle financing.
